title: Set pieces are Arsenal's quiet edge again
excerpt: Newcastle concede more from corners than any top-half side. Arsenal have scored four from dead balls already.
body: Arsenal have scored four set-piece goals already, and Newcastle have conceded more from corners than any other top-half side. The duel between Arsenal's near-post runners and Newcastle's zonal marking is the clearest edge on the pitch.

In open play this is closer than the table suggests: Newcastle press well for an hour, but their away output has dropped sharply (three goals in three). I expect Arsenal to have the ball and the better chances without it being comfortable.
Watch the Newcastle left-back. If he starts, they're far better at stopping Arsenal's right-sided overloads.

title: Atalanta's press is the variable that matters
excerpt: If Inter's back three can play through the first line, the space behind Atalanta's wing-backs is enormous. If not, expect a scrappy, stop-start game.
body: Atalanta's man-to-man press is the variable that decides this. Inter's back three are comfortable on the ball, but nobody has played through Atalanta's first line cleanly this season.

If Inter do get through it, the space behind Atalanta's wing-backs is enormous, and Inter's forwards are the best in Serie A at attacking it. If they can't, expect a scrappy, stop-start game with chances at both ends.
That uncertainty is why my conviction is low. This is a game to read after twenty minutes, not before kickoff.

title: Villa's high line vs Anfield's tempo
excerpt: Villa hold one of the league's highest defensive lines. Against Liverpool's runners in behind, that's a structural risk worth tracking.
body: Villa hold one of the league's highest defensive lines. Against Liverpool's runners in behind, that's a structural risk worth tracking.
Villa have been good at Villa Park but have kept just one clean sheet. Anfield's tempo in the first half-hour has broken better-organised sides this season.
Liverpool should win the territory battle comfortably; the question is whether Villa's counter can punish a Liverpool side that commits full-backs high.
